MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Department - Program 


Join Monash Health as a Quality Systems & Insights Analyst and play a key role in improving the safety and quality of care for one of Victoria's largest health services. Combining data analytics, quality systems expertise and clinical governance insight, you'll transform information into meaningful action, support organisation wide quality systems, and help leaders make decisions that improve patient outcomes. If you enjoy solving problems, working with data, optimising systems, and partnering with stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and positive change, this is an opportunity to make a real impact across a complex and dynamic healthcare environment.


The Quality & Clinical Governance Unit plays a central role in supporting Monash Health's commitment to delivering safe, effective and high-quality care. The team provides leadership, systems and oversight that strengthen clinical governance, quality improvement, patient safety and organisational learning across the health service.


The Quality Insights & Systems team manages and optimises key quality systems, supports the collection and analysis of clinical governance information, and provides meaningful insights that help leaders identify risks, monitor performance and drive continuous improvement. Working collaboratively with programs and services across Monash Health, the team supports evidence-based decision-making and initiatives that enhance patient outcomes and organisational performance.







About the Role 








This is a part time ongoing position located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, you will work under the leadership of the Quality Insights & Systems manager and collaborate closely with the broader Quality & Clinical Governance team and stakeholders across Monash Health.


This is an exciting opportunity for a quality systems and data professional who enjoys combining analytical thinking, systems administration and continuous improvement to support safer patient care. The role is responsible for maintaining and optimising key organisational quality systems while developing meaningful clinical governance insights that inform decision-making and improvement initiatives.










Key responsibilities include:



Administering and optimising Monash Health's quality systems, including incident management, document control and audit platforms.


Analysing clinical quality data and other information sources to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement. 


Developing and delivering clinical governance reports, dashboards and insights that support leaders and teams. 


Providing user support, education and training to improve staff capability in quality systems and data interpretation. 


Working with internal stakeholders, external vendors and partner teams to enhance system performance, data integrity and governance processes. 


Contributing to quality improvement initiatives, system enhancements and process optimisation projects.









This role will involve working with stakeholders across multiple Monash Health sites. A hybrid working arrangement may be available in line with team and organisational requirements.







About You 


To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring demonstrated experience in systems administration, data analysis and quality improvement within a complex organisational environment. 


You will be someone who is curious, analytical and solutions-focused, with the ability to translate data into meaningful insights and build strong collaborative relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.


You will have:




Experience administering, supporting or improving systems and processes in a complex organisation. 


Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and communicate actionable insights. 


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including report writing, presentations and development of guidance materials.


Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building capabilities. 


Experience providing education, training and support to end-users.


High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining data integrity and quality. 


Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset. 


Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.


Experience using RiskMan, PROMPT, MARS or similar systems will be highly regarded.



Mandatory Requirements:




Degree qualification in health, quality, business management, data analytics or a related discipline.


Current right to work in Australia. 


Ability to obtain and maintain required screening checks, including National Police Check and Working with Children Check.


Current Victorian Driver's Licence is highly desirable



 
Desirable:




Knowledge of quality, safety and clinical governance principles within a health service environment. 


Experience working in a complex healthcare organisation.This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to Monash Health's quality and safety agenda, helping to strengthen systems, generate valuable organisational insights and support continuous improvement across one of Australia's largest health services. 










For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Linda Chuang, Qualtiy Insights & Systems Manager via linda.chuang@monashhealth.org

result.description:
Dubbo Grain Packing (DGP)
Grain Storage & Handling Site, Trangie, NSW 2823

Full Time General Clerk
$98,000 per annum plus superannuation

Summary
The General Clerk provides administrative and clerical support to the operations of Dubbo
Grain Packing (DGP). The position is responsible for maintaining records, processing
documentation, data entry, preparing correspondence, coordinating office activities, and
supporting grain storage and handling operations through efficient administrative services.

Duties and Responsibilities

General Administrative Support
•	Perform a range of clerical and administrative duties to support site operations.
•	Prepare, process and file business documents, forms and correspondence.
•	Maintain electronic and physical filing systems.
•	Receive, sort and distribute incoming mail and communications.
•	Assist management with routine administrative tasks.

Record Keeping and Data Entry
•	Enter and update operational information into company databases and record systems.
•	Maintain records relating to grain receivals, dispatches and inventory movements.
•	Verify information for accuracy and completeness.
•	Retrieve records and documents as requested by management.
•	Ensure records are maintained in accordance with company procedures.

Document Preparation
•	Prepare routine reports, spreadsheets, forms and correspondence.
•	Compile operational data for management reporting purposes.
•	Assist with preparation of meeting agendas, minutes and administrative documentation.
•	Maintain document registers and administrative records.

Customer and Stakeholder Liaison
•	Respond to routine enquiries from customers, suppliers, transport operators and
•	contractors.
•	Direct enquiries to appropriate personnel when required.
•	Provide administrative support to visitors and site personnel.
•	Maintain professional communication with internal and external stakeholders.

Operational Administration Support
•	Assist with processing grain receival and dispatch documentation.
•	Maintain weighbridge and transport records.
•	Support scheduling and coordination of administrative activities during harvest periods.
•	Assist operational staff with document management and record maintenance.

Compliance Administration
•	Maintain records required for workplace health and safety, training and compliance
•	purposes.
•	Assist with preparation of documentation for audits and inspections.
•	Ensure administrative records are current, accurate and readily accessible.
•	Support implementation of company policies and procedures.

Reporting
•	Prepare routine administrative and operational reports.
•	Compile statistical information and summaries as requested by management.
•	Assist with monitoring and reporting of administrative activities.

Skills and Competencies
•	Strong administrative and clerical skills.
•	Accurate data entry and record management capability.
•	Sound computer and office software skills.
•	Strong organisational and time management skills.
•	Effective written and verbal communication skills.
•	Attention to detail and accuracy.

Qualifications and Experience
•	Certificate III, Certificate IV or higher qualification in Business Administration or a related field; or
•	At least one year of relevant clerical or administrative experience.
•	At least 12 months experience with a program called Agtech and Agri-digital.


Applications open on 2 July 2026 and close on 1 August 2026

•	High level of integrity, confidentiality and professionalism when handling sensitive financial information. 
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment. 
•	Knowledge of inventory control, internal controls, budgeting and audit processes is highly regarded.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     ASO3 PAS Data Integrity Officer - PAS





Job no: 941831

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide Metro Northern

Categories: Administration, Business and Management




 

Northern Adelaide Local Health Network - Corporate Services - Elizabeth South

Salary: $74,095 - $78,694 per annum - plus Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice Benefits - ASO3

Ongoing Full-Time

About the Role:

As a PAS (Patient Administrative System) Data Integrity Officer, you will play a critical role in maintaining the accuracy, quality and integrity of patient information within the Sunrise Electronic Medical Record (EMR) across the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network. Working within the Patient Administrative System Data Integrity Unit (PAS DIU), you will help ensure patient registration, demographic and activity data meets State and Federal data standards, supporting safe patient care, accurate reporting and organisational performance.

Working closely with Health Information Management Services, clinical teams, administrative staff, the Registry Integrity Unit and other stakeholders, you will provide expert advice on patient registration practices, investigate and resolve data discrepancies, monitor key performance indicators, and contribute to ongoing quality improvement initiatives. You will also support staff education and provide guidance on data standards, procedures and best practice to strengthen data quality across the network.

The PAS DIU provides leadership in the management, education and administration of PAS in Sunrise EMR, with expertise in SA Health data management, patient registration, data quality and integrity, health information management, and patient activity data capture associated with Casemix and Activity Based Funding (ABF). In this role, you will contribute to these functions through the management of duplicate registrations, data validation, auditing, reporting, troubleshooting data quality issues and supporting compliance with Admitted Patient Care (APC) requirements and Consumer Identification Standards.

About You:

You are a highly organised and detail-focused professional with a passion for data accuracy and quality. You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, the ability to manage competing priorities, and a commitment to maintaining confidentiality when working with sensitive information.

With excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach, you build effective relationships with a wide range of stakeholders while providing expert support to improve patient registration practices, data quality and compliance across the health service.

This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented professional who enjoys analysing information, solving complex problems and making a meaningful contribution to the quality, accuracy and reliability of health information that underpins patient care, service planning and funding outcomes.

About Us:

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management.

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community.

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services:

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services.

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services.

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care.

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings.

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites.

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains.

Benefits of working at NALHN:

From salary packaging to flexible working arrangements, a large range of opportunities for movement and career progression, you'll find there are lots of benefits of working with Northern Adelaide Local Health Network.

Salary packaging is an option for saving money by paying for some of your everyday expenses from your salary before it is taxed.

Relocation assistance may be available for successful applicants from interstate or overseas.

NALHN supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if you have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working including part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check.

Checks: 

National Police Check (National Police Certificate) for general probity screening - apply to any of the accredited bodies approved to offer a service direct to the public. Accreditation is provided by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission. See our National Police Certificate accredited bodies page for l
